lines.text: Memorial General Hospital - Department of Inpatient Medicine
CLINICAL DOCUMENTATION — NARRATIVE INPATIENT DISCHARGE SUMMARY V1
Patient: James Lopez | MRN: PAT-60001 | DOB: 1965-04-05 | Gender: Male | Doc ID: NARRATIVE_0001
Encounter Date: 2025-02-01 | Discharge/Note Date: 2025-02-03 | Provider: Dr. Lisa Cuddy, MD
CHIEF COMPLAINT
The patient presented with worsening bilateral lower extremity edema and dyspnea on exertion.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
The patient is a 62-year-old male with a medical history pertinent for hypertension and dyslipidemia who presented for
evaluation of worsening bilateral lower extremity edema and dyspnea on exertion. Symptoms began approximately four
days prior to admission and escalated in severity. On presentation to the emergency department, initial diagnostic
evaluation demonstrated that hemoglobin was 14 g/dL. Concurrently, serum chemistry was notable for a bun of 29.3 mg/dL
(HIGH). Vital signs upon arrival were stable, and the patient was admitted to the inpatient general medicine service.
HOSPITAL COURSE
During the hospital course, the inpatient team initiated targeted management. The patient received Amoxicillin 250 mg orally
every 8 hours for 7 days with good clinical tolerance. Serial assessments revealed gradual resolution of presenting
symptoms. Prior to planned discharge, repeat laboratory testing confirmed that glucose stabilized at 87.9 mg/dL. The patient
was ambulating without assistance and tolerating a regular diet.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS
The patient was discharged home in stable clinical condition with instructions to take Lisinopril 40 mg orally every morning,
and Atorvastatin 10 mg by mouth every evening. Medication reconciliation was completed and all questions regarding
dosing schedules were answered.
DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS & FOLLOW-UP
The patient was advised to follow up with their primary care physician within 7 to 10 days. Return precautions for chest pain,
recurrent shortness of breath, or fever were provided and understood.
